title: Shohei Ohtani will be in Dodgers' Game 3 lineup against Brewers
summary: Shohei Ohtani will be in the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup for Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers
story: Shohei Ohtani will be in the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup for Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers
LOS ANGELES -- LOS ANGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani will be in the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup for Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday night.
Manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday that Ohtani will bat anywhere from second to sixth with the two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers losing the first two games of the best-of-seven series.

“He was very convicted that he is onto something mechanically (with his swing),” Roberts said. “He was adamant that he can help us. He’s well enough to help us win a baseball game, so that’s all I needed to hear.”
Ohtani is hitting .150 (3 for 20) over six postseason games. He has seven strikeouts, three walks and one stolen base with no home runs, no RBIs and an OPS of .411.
He hasn’t homered since Aug. 18 at Colorado.

Ohtani admitted before the NLDS against Atlanta that he’s not 100% healthy from right biceps and left knee issues that bothered him the last the last few months of the regular season. He has appeared visibly uncomfortable at the plate while flailing at pitches.

“The symptoms have subdued a lot,” Ohtani said Tuesday through a translator while making an unscheduled appearance in the off-day interview room. “The symptoms shouldn’t be the reason why I can’t hit, and even if the injuries happen by accident, I take full responsibility.”
Roberts spoke to Ohtani before the team worked out at Dodger Stadium, where Ohtani took on-field batting practice, something he rarely does during the regular season.

Roberts said their conversation wasn’t about benching the Japanese superstar, but rather offering him time off similar to Freddie Freeman during the postseason in 2024. Freeman had a sprained ankle and bone bruise, and took three days off spanning the NL Division Series and NLCS before earning World Series MVP honors.

“Over the course of this long season, there’s only really a short period of time when my mechanics is completely in sync,” Ohtani said. “So it’s just really kind of just going back and forth, finding the right parts of the swing and managing just the different parts of the swing. It’s a constant, ongoing process that’s headed in the right direction.”
Ohtani led the Dodgers to a four-game NLCS sweep of Milwaukee last year, when the Brewers hit a measly .118 against LA's pitching.

He was 5 for 14 (.357) with three home runs, four walks and five strikeouts as NLCS MVP — all three homers came in a memorable Game 4 clinch in which he also struck out 10 as a pitcher. He had a 1.643 OPS and 1.143 slugging percentage.

“We remember vividly at this time last year that he maybe had the best baseball game ever played the day he pitched against us and hit a home run every time up, it seemed like,” Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. “You can’t forget that, his capabilities. But you still have to go at him.”
Ohtani is known for hitting homers but the offensively starved Dodgers would take any kind of production from him at this point.
“In this big moment, we’re listening to Shohei, and we’re going to support the crap out of him and believe in him," Roberts said, "and that’s it.”
Two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell starts for Los Angeles against Robert Gasser of the Brewers in a matchup of left-handers on Wednesday.
The Dodgers will be looking to get considerably more innings out of Snell than in his last start on Oct. 4.

He lasted 3 2/3 innings, giving up one run, three hits, walking five and striking out five, in a 3-2 loss in Game 2 of the NLDS against Atlanta. He didn't speak to media afterward and has kept a low profile since then.

“Just a lot of time talking to myself, figuring out where I need to get to, where I’m at,” he said. “Watching two games against Milwaukee, just kind of game planning, seeing what I can expose, what they’re doing really well. Just trying to figure them out.”

Brewers center fielder Garrett Mitchell grew up in Orange County as a Los Angeles Angels fan. His family had season tickets in left field. He went to high school with the son of Angels star Garret Anderson.

“Got to have some good conversations with him, take some blasts into the past and talk about memories,” Mitchell said. “I was a shortstop when I was a kid, too. So I enjoyed watching David Eckstein and Adam Kennedy, and I also have a personal relationship with Adam Kennedy as well.”
Mitchell said the way the Angels played reminds him of how the Brewers approach games.

“Guys who maybe aren’t the greatest or the best on the field but know what they’ve got to do and know their roles and grind and compete to the best of their abilities,” he said. “That’s what it takes, it’s a team effort.” ___

title: Longhorns and Gators clash with bruised bodies and egos needing win to keep their seasons on track
summary: Three weeks ago, the Texas-Florida matchup looked like a potential blockbuster
story: Three weeks ago, the Texas-Florida matchup looked like a potential blockbuster
AUSTIN, Texas -- Three weeks ago, the Texas-Florida matchup looked like a blockbuster.
The Longhorns were No. 1 behind quarterback Arch Manning. The Gators were storming up the rankings behind first-year coach Jon Sumrall and igniting the chomp in the Swamp.
Those were good times. Both teams now limp into Saturday's game in Austin with bruised bodies and egos, and carrying a whiff of desperation for a win to keep the season from unraveling.

Seventh-ranked Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) is back home after a deflating loss to unranked archrival Oklahoma in Dallas, where Manning threw a pair of costly fourth-quarter interceptions. The Gators (4-2, 2-2) are probably glad to hit the road after a getting run out of the Swamp last week by South Carolina.
Texas was shaken by the loss, but is still in the hunt for the SEC championship and the College Football Playoff.
Manning said this week he's looking forward to a rematch with the Gators, who handed Texas a humbling defeat last year. That loss that played a big role in the Longhorns' not reaching the playoff.
“Obviously a new (Florida) coach and they have some new players, but it left a bad taste in my mouth,” Manning said.

The Gators looked great when they blasted Ole Miss last month. But those home cheers turned into some boos in last week's 38-19 loss to South Carolina. The defeat exposed just how far a program with talented players still has to go.
“We’re a work in progress," Sumrall said. "Sometimes our progress is dysfunctional.”

Florida starting quarterback Aaron Philo was listed as questionable Thursday because of a shoulder injury that limited his practice time. If he doesn't play, sophomore Trammel Jones would make his first career start. The Gators are hopeful they will have star receiver Vernell Brown III after missing the last two games with a knee injury.

The Gators sacked Manning six times last season and pass protection was a problem for Texas all year. Manning says his protection is much improved, but he's still been sacked eight times the last two games. Manning blames himself for some of that.
“I haven't helped them out, getting the ball out (quicker)," he said. "I've been taking some unnecessary sacks.”

Texas special teams have been a huge problem of late. In the last two weeks, Texas gave up its first punt return touchdown since 2013 and its first punt block for a TD since 2009. Sarkisian has said he won't take special teams coaching duties away from assistant Jeff Banks.

The Longhorns aren't scaring anyone on offense and Sarkisian has come under fire for his play calling. Texas ranks 12th in the SEC in total offense at 379 yards per game. But the Gators' defensive struggles have been even worse. Florida ranks last in the SEC in total defense and had more than 20 missed tackles last week against South Carolina.
(Corrects spelling of Jon Sumrall's first name in original version)

title: Miami freshman golfer Kai Trump, President Trump's granddaughter, says she had wrist surgery
summary: Miami freshman golfer Kai Trump, the granddaughter of President Donald Trump, has undergone surgery for a left wrist injury
story: Miami freshman golfer Kai Trump, the granddaughter of President Donald Trump, has undergone surgery for a left wrist injury
CORAL GABLES, Fla. -- Kai Trump's freshman season on Miami's golf team has hit a snag.

The granddaughter of President Donald Trump revealed on social media Wednesday that she recently had surgery to repair a left wrist injury. She did not reveal the severity and said the injury happened during her first tournament of the season.

“While I had hoped to avoid surgery, after talks with my family, coaches, and athletic training staff I know I made the best decision for my long-term health and my future in the game I love,” she wrote on social media. “It’s certainly not how I envisioned the next few months, but sometimes the journey takes an unexpected turn, and I’m choosing to embrace this one with patience, and a whole lot of determination.”

Kai Trump is one of nine players on Miami's roster. The Hurricanes, as a team, have two tournament wins and one runner-up finish in three events this season — currently holding the No. 7 spot in the national rankings.
“For now, it’s all about healing, and trusting the process,” she wrote in her post. “I can’t wait to be back with my team, doing what I love."

title: With the Jaguars on the rise, UK fans nervous about team's plan to reevaluate its London strategy
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to play their 16th London game when they face the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium on Sunday
story: The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to play their 16th London game when they face the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium on Sunday
LONDON -- Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence cited London’s “history and the feel and charm” on Sunday after a dramatic victory over the Philadelphia Eagles.
“I feel like we have a strong connection and tie to London,” Lawrence said. “We’ve been playing here for a long time. Who knows if that will change?”
Indeed, it’s quite possible it could.

The Jaguars said before the season that they’re going to “totally reevaluate” their London strategy. Their economic motivation to play in London each year — usually at Wembley Stadium like they’ll do Sunday against the Houston Texans — will decrease when their stadium renovation in Jacksonville is complete, expected in time for the 2028 season.

Under owner Shad Khan, the Jaguars were early adopters of the NFL’s international push and started playing annual games in the British capital in 2013. Khan also owns London-based Fulham in the Premier League.
Jags fans in the U.K. are hoping the team doesn’t disappear.
They’ve supported them through the lean years — until 2025, the Jags had never brought a winning record to London.
But now, expectations are sky high.

“We’re totally bought in,” Scottish fan Keir Robinson said Sunday before kickoff at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where the Jags beat the Eagles 19-17. “What Liam Coen is doing just now is incredible. This is our time. I think we are playoff-bound, could be Super Bowl-bound.”
Robinson and his wife, Julie, took a 7 a.m. flight from Edinburgh to London for the game.
As for the future?
“If they were here every second year, that would be big for us,” he said. “If they never come back, five years down the line am I still a Jags fan? I don’t know.”
Another fan, John Rawson of Dorset in southwest England, added “it would be a shame” if the team changed course.
The Jaguars have not made any announcements about their long-term future in London.

Any potential big changes might not take effect until 2028, when their stadium is complete. The Jags will move most of their home games to Orlando next season, when they'll still have the option of playing three home games in London.

Team President Mark Lamping told the team’s flagship radio broadcaster during the preseason that “our commitment to London is year to year” and that it's time to "totally reevaluate our London strategy.”

In a statement to The Associated Press, Lamping said the Jags “were pioneers in the league’s international strategy by first committing to one home game annually in London beginning with the 2013 season.”

"Our year-round presence in London since then has been a major plus for the league, the U.K. and our home market of Jacksonville, which has realized business and tourism benefits made possible only due to our immersion in London," he added.
Sunday's game will be Jacksonville's 16th in London.
Britain has a well-developed NFL fanbase with support for a variety of teams. But they’re not all Jacksonville fans, which means there’s some fatigue with the Jags coming year after year.
Matt Cullen, an Englishman who supports the New York Jets said: “Fans are a little bit bored of the Jags now.”
That was before Sunday’s drama at Tottenham, but stats back up his sentiment.

The Jags ranked No. 28 for most-watched teams on NFL Game Pass in Britain and Ireland in 2025. Jacksonville was also among the lesser-searched NFL teams by U.K. fans in 2025, according to analytics company Hyperset Group, based on Google search data.
Still, attendance at three of the past four Jaguars games at Wembley exceeded 86,000. Tickets were still available this week for Sunday’s game but far fewer than were available a few weeks ago.
The Jags and nine other teams have NFL-approved marketing rights in the U.K. Few can match Jacksonville’s presence and longevity in Britain, but they’re certainly looking for new supporters.
The Minnesota Vikings held a scavenger hunt in London last week. Fans located purple envelopes downtown and won Justin Jefferson jerseys.
Of the teams with U.K.-specific social media accounts, the Vikings have the most Instagram followers (almost 43,000), followed by the Jaguars and the Bears. The Jags are way ahead on X.

The Chicago Bears this month are on a “U.K. grand tour” with events in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. The Bears’ popularity here dates to a 1986 preseason game at the original Wembley Stadium. Mike Ditka was Chicago’s coach and defensive lineman William “The Refrigerator” Perry got the headlines.

title: Swanson scores first goal since the Olympics in USWNT's 2-2 draw with Spain
summary: Mallory Swanson her first goal since the game-winner in the gold medal match at the 2024 Olympics in the 86th minute to pull the United States into a 2-2 draw with Spain on Tuesday night
story: Mallory Swanson her first goal since the game-winner in the gold medal match at the 2024 Olympics in the 86th minute to pull the United States into a 2-2 draw with Spain on Tuesday night
CHESTER, Pa. -- Mallory Swanson scored her first goal since the gold medal match at the 2024 Olympics in the 86th minute to pull the United States into a 2-2 draw with Spain on Tuesday night.
Ashley Sanchez also scored early in the second half for the United States after first-half goals from Alexia Putellas and Salma Paralluelo gave Spain a 2-0 lead.
“I mean, this mentality of this team has always been you stay with it,” said Swanson, who subbed into the game in the second half. “That's what this crest means.”

It was the second of two friendly matches against Spain, the 2023 Women's World Cup winners. Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro scored in the first 14 minutes to lift Spain to a 2-0 victory in the first match on Saturday in Washington D.C.
Spain, ranked No. 1 in the world, has already qualified for the World Cup next summer in Brazil. The United States was using the matches as preparation for World Cup qualifying later this year.

Putellas, the two-time Ballon d'Or winner, was making her 150th appearance for Spain. She put Spain in front in the 27th minute with her 43rd international goal, a tap-in at the far post off a feed from Clara Pinedo.

Some five minutes later, U.S. goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce misplayed the ball up the field and Spain pounced. Putellas sent the ball forward to Paralluelo, whose blast hit the crossbar and fell into the goal to make it 2-0.
It was the first time the United States has given up two first-half goals to an opponent in consecutive matches since 2011.

The U.S. pulled back a goal early in the second when Sanchez found a gap and scored to the far post. Sanchez was making her first start in for the United States since Oct. 30, 2024, against Argentina.
Sanchez has been on a tear for the North Carolina Courage in the National Women’s Soccer League, scoring a league-leading 20 goals in 27 games.

In the final minutes, Michelle Cooper took a long ball from Kate Del Fava and sent it over to Swanson for the volley. Swanson's last goal gave the United States a 1-0 victory over Brazil at the Paris Games. She spent 2025 on maternity leave for the birth of her daughter.
“I think one of our big things in the game plan was just like finding those spaces in the box and being clinical in the box, and you could see that,” Swanson said.
Lily Yohannes nearly scored for the United States in stoppage time, but Misa Rodríguez made a diving save.

“Obviously we always want to win, that's the type of team that we are and I think if we had 20 more minutes we definitely probably would have won,” Sanchez said. “But it was good just to get a tie against a team like that and come back from 2-nil down.”

Spain dominated despite missing some of its biggest players, including Aitana Bonmati, who is still working her way back from a broken leg. Vicky Lopez, Mariona Caldentey and goalkeeper Cata Coll were all also unavailable for the matches because of injuries.
Chicago Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson, Mallory Swanson's husband, and tennis player Ben Shelton, who is dating Trinity Rodman, were among those in the crowd at Subaru Park.

title: Jury finds Tyreek Hill liable for 2 battery counts, awards $500,000 to the NFL star's estranged wife
summary: A Miami jury has found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro
story: A Miami jury has found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro

MIAMI -- A Miami jury on Tuesday found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro — ending the high-profile civil trial involving the NFL wide receiver and his estranged wife.

Hill, who has played for the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs and Miami Dolphins, was found liable for two counts of battery — one stemming from an incident in January 2024, and another from April 2025. The jury awarded Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages but did not award her punitive damages.
The jury found Hill, 32, not liable for eight other counts that included battery, assault and continuing domestic violence.

The trial involved allegations of abuse made by Vaccaro, 30, who on the stand described instances in which Hill allegedly pulled her hair and “treated me like I was, just, a man.” Hill took the stand last week and mostly denied what he called “false allegations” made by his estranged wife, while saying in one instance he shoved Vaccaro and “created a hole in the wall."
Hill, wearing a dark polo shirt on Tuesday, embraced one of his attorneys and shook hands with others following the verdict before leaving the courtroom by himself.

It wasn't immediately clear what the verdict means for Hill's return to the NFL. He is still working his way back from a dislocated knee and torn ligaments suffered in September 2025 while he was with the Dolphins, but his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has indicated that he could be ready to play by November.

title: Shiffrin takes a more off-script approach in shifting focus beyond slalom and in Year 2 of podcast
summary: Mikaela Shiffrin is embracing an "exploration season" in her 16th year on the World Cup circuit
story: Mikaela Shiffrin is embracing an "exploration season" in her 16th year on the World Cup circuit
Mikaela Shiffrin is embracing an off-script approach in what the ski racer has dubbed her “exploration season.”

That includes on the mountain, where the three-time Olympic champion will prioritize training in giant slalom and super-G over her signature slalom event. It also extends to the microphone, with her plan to be even more free-flowing in interviews on her podcast, "What’s the Point.”
Just a way to feed her curiosity as she enters her 16th season on the World Cup circuit and second hosting her show. In her eyes, a speedy race and a seamless podcast have a common thread — cadence.

“When I’m skiing my best, it feels like a dance,” Shiffrin wrote in an email to The Associated Press as her 12-episode podcast kicked off Wednesday and featured media personality/fellow podcaster Kylie Kelce. "The turns link together and I stop thinking about them. A great episode has a similar rhythm. One question flows into the next, I might go ‘off script’ — it just feels natural and not forced. Then afterward the guest says something like, ‘That was such a fun conversation, let’s talk again soon.’ That’s my version of seeing green (signifying the fastest time) at the finish.”

From now until March, Shiffrin will feature episodes in which she interviews top names from around the sports world, including figure skater Ilia Malinin, rugby player Ilona Maher, tennis great Iga Swiatek and sportscaster Mike Tirico. The theme is what drives them toward success.
It’s a question she's pondered, too.

The six-time overall World Cup champion will focus her attention more on the GS and super-G this season. Sure, she will still compete in slalom, her top event. But she wanted to branch out after a season in which she won nine of 10 World Cup slalom events, along with capturing gold at the Milan Cortina Olympics.
A little bit of a scary decision, “because the safe choice was obvious,” the 31-year-old from Colorado said.

“I was coming off a successful slalom season, and if you only look at results, staying focused on slalom made the most sense,” she added. “But after 16 years on the World Cup, I felt a real curiosity pulling me toward GS and super-G, and I’ve learned to trust that feeling. Making peace with it came from being clear with myself about why I was doing it. It’s not about caring less or working less. It’s about recovering better, training with more intention, and racing slalom when I’m prepared for it. Slalom isn’t going anywhere.”

Shiffrin and her fellow racers push out of the start gate on Oct. 24 with a giant slalom competition in Soelden, Austria. Shiffrin said her first slalom race will be in Killington, Vermont, over Thanksgiving weekend.
“I’m keeping the door open,” Shiffrin said of her racing plans. "We’re calling this the exploration season, and I think that framing is what let me exhale.”
As for podcasting, she’s finding her groove. Last season, her guests included her fiancé, Norwegian ski racer Aleksander Aamodt Kilde, and gymnast Simone Biles, winner of seven Olympic gold medals.

“I learned that listening is a skill you train, just like skiing,” said Shiffrin, whose podcast launched in October 2025 in partnership with financial group Stifel. “In Season 1, I’d sometimes be so focused on getting to my next question that I’d miss the best thing a guest said. ... So in Year 2 I’m prepping less of a script and more of a direction. I also learned that I don’t need to be the expert in the room.”
Her plans going forward — and leading into the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps — remain fluid, in racing and podcasting.

“Whether I’m in the start gate, in the crowd cheering on former competitors and teammates, or even hosting live episodes of 'What’s the Point,’ I’ll tackle it with the same passion and curiosity I bring today," Shiffrin said. "What I can promise is that as long as I’m skiing, it’ll be because I want to, not because I feel I have to.”

title: Barcola's hat trick helps Liverpool rout LASK, Feyenoord fights back in Champions League
summary: Bradley Barcola has scored a hat trick and Liverpool has coasted to a 6-3 win at Austria’s LASK in the Champions League
story: Bradley Barcola has scored a hat trick and Liverpool has coasted to a 6-3 win at Austria’s LASK in the Champions League
LINZ, Austria -- Bradley Barcola scored a hat trick as Liverpool coasted to a 6-3 win at Austria’s LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday.
They were his first goals for the club since joining from European champion Paris Saint-Germain in the offseason.
Ronald Araújo also got his first Liverpool goal as he broke the deadlock with a header from a corner, less than two minutes before Barcola scored in the 24th from a lay-off by Lewis Koumas.
Ryan Gravenberch struck the post before Barcola got his second in the 37th, finishing with aplomb after being played through by Florian Wirtz.
Jeremie Frimpong, one of the smallest players on the field, headed Liverpool’s fourth in off the right post in the 51st.
Robert Ljubičić pulled a goal back in the 63rd, a minute after going on as a substitute, before Frimpong gave Barcola a simple tap-in to complete his hat trick in the 66th.
Koumas was left free to get Liverpool’s sixth six minutes later – it was the 21-year-old forward's first Liverpool goal.
But Florian Flecker – another LASK substitute – got the biggest cheer when he scored his team’s second with a diving header in the 74th, four minutes before he got another to complete the scoring.
Liverpool coach Andoni Iraola dropped Virgil van Dijk to the substitutes’ bench with French defender Jérémy Jacquet starting. The Dutch star replaced Jacquet for the last half hour or so.
Anis Hadj Moussa scored twice as Dutch leader Feyenoord came from behind to beat visiting Como 3-2 in the other early game.
Assane Diao gave Como the lead with the team’s first shot in the 18th minute after outmuscling Javi López on the right and firing inside the far post.
But Gjivai Zechiël replied two minutes later with a spectacular shot, and Algeria winger Hadj Moussa scored early in the second half before sealing the result in the 82nd.
Tasos Douvikas scored Como's consolation in stoppage time.
Scandal-hit Manchester City was hosting fellow big spender PSG later for its first European game since being charged with financial rule-breaking over nearly a decade in the Premier League.

Also later, Real Madrid was visiting Roma for coach José Mourinho’s return, Bodø/Glimt was playing Borussia Dortmund, Real Betis was entertaining Porto, Fenerbahçe was visiting Aston Villa, Stuttgart traveled to Slovan Bratislava, and Ukraine’s Shakhtar Donetsk was hosting AEK Athens at Chelsea’s ground in London.

title: Shai Hope’s 102 gives West Indies series-leveling win over India in fourth cricket T20
summary: Shai Hope has set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2
story: Shai Hope has set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2
HYDERABAD, India -- Shai Hope set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs Wednesday in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2.
Hope hit nine sixes and four fours in his third T20 century – the most for a West Indies batter – as the visitors piled up 247-3 in 20 overs. India had won the toss and opted to bowl.
It was the second-highest first innings total in T20s against India, trailing England’s 257-3 in Southampton this year.
In reply, Sanju Samson hit 56 off 23 balls but India was down to 130-5 and the chase never took off. It finished with 223 in 19.3 overs.
Keemo Paul picked 5-41 for his second five-wicket haul in T20s.
Bengaluru will host the deciding T20 on Saturday.
Put into bat, Hope gave West Indies a flying by putting on 52 off 26 balls with Jewel Andrew (21). Axar Patel trapped Andrew lbw in the fifth over but West Indies still got 79-1 in the powerplay.
Hope then added another 58 off 24 balls with Shimron Hetmyer, reaching 50 off 28 balls with the help of five sixes. He sped to a second hundred in the series with another four sixes.
Hope also became only the fifth batter to score multiple hundreds in a bilateral T20 series. Overall, it was his fourth hundred in seven innings across ODIs and T20s on this tour.
He wasn’t finished, despite Prince Yadav sending back Hetmyer for 33, while Rovman Powell scored 24.
Sherfane Rutherford scored 49 not out off 26 balls to provide the final flourish, hitting four fours and three sixes, as West Indies breached 200.

Hope and Rutherford added 91 off only 43 balls, as India served a slow over-rate penalty in the final over. Nitish Reddy gave away 19 runs in the 20th, with Hope reaching his century with a six off the last ball.
In reply, Samson hit four sixes to give India a quick start. He and Abhishek Sharma (29) added 60 off 25 balls as India scored 80-2 in the powerplay.
Keemo Paul struck twice in the fifth over – Samson was out caught at square leg on the first ball and then three balls later, Ishan Kishan was caught at deep mid wicket for six.
India also lost skipper Shreyas Iyer (16) before the halfway mark, and was down to 97-3.
Abhishek Sharma didn’t get going, scoring 29 off 24 balls, with three fours and a six. His dismissal was the turning point – he was caught off Gudakesh Motie at long off in the 12th over.
Motie also had Naman Dhir stumped for a golden duck.
Tilak Varma fought hard with 43 off 25 balls along with Nitish Reddy’s cameo (41 off 20 balls) but it went in vain.
Paul picked three wickets in the 19th over to wrap up the innings.

title: Brewers stun Dodgers with back-to-back homers in 7th inning and take 3-0 lead in NLCS with 6-2 win
summary: Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh inning to help the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series
story: Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh inning to help the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series
LOS ANGELES -- The Milwaukee Brewers hit the second-fewest home runs in baseball during the regular season, even as they topped the majors with 103 wins.
Maybe they were saving their biggest swings for the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell launched back-to-back homers off Blake Snell as Milwaukee regained the lead in the seventh inning, and the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to build a 3-0 cushion in the National League Championship Series.

Jackson Chourio also went deep on the first pitch of the game to help the Brewers close within one win of their first NL pennant. Milwaukee was in the American League when the franchise reached its only World Series, a seven-game loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982.
“Job’s not finished yet,” Mitchell said.
Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium, where the Brewers can become the first major league club to complete a postseason sweep after getting swept by that same opponent in the previous postseason.
Los Angeles took all four games against Milwaukee in the NLCS last year.
The Dodgers had just gone ahead 2-1 in the sixth before getting stunned. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination.
“All three games we’ve played so far, and hopefully that continues, where just every time they score, we come back and score,” Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. “That’s not easy to do in baseball.”
It was the fifth comeback victory in seven games this postseason for the Brewers, who have never beaten Los Angeles in three previous playoff series.
The only other time the Dodgers trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.
The lone team in big league history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven postseason series was the Boston Red Sox in the 2004 AL Championship Series against the New York Yankees.
“We’ve won four in a row a number of times this year,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “We've got to win tomorrow. That’s our only focus.”

Coming into the seventh, Snell had retired 14 batters in a row. The first pitch of the game thrown by the two-time Cy Young Award winner was hit for a home run by Chourio, and his last pitch was Mitchell's solo shot.

Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the inning and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412-foot drive to right field on the 11th pitch of the at-bat for a 3-2 lead as most of the players in Milwaukee's dugout came onto the field to celebrate.
“I was looking for a fastball, and I didn’t want to miss it,” said Bauers, who had a team-leading 26 of Milwaukee's 154 regular-season homers.
It was his latest relentless plate appearance, too, after Bauers drew a 12-pitch walk from Yoshinobu Yamamoto that helped the Brewers go ahead early in Game 2.
“I think what changed for me this year was I stopped caring about results,” Bauers said. “I started caring about competing. I started caring about being in the moment and getting out of my own way.”
Watching Bauers work over Snell was “super sick,” Mitchell said.
And then it was his turn.

Mitchell's drive traveled 428 feet to right-center. That chased Snell, who hadn't given up a home run in 46 1/3 innings this year entering the game. It was the first time in his career he served up back-to-back homers to left-handed hitters and only the second time he gave up multiple longballs to left-handed batters in one game.

Bauers and Mitchell became just the third pair of left-handed hitters with consecutive postseason home runs off the same left-handed pitcher. Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper did it for Philadelphia against Atlanta reliever Dylan Lee in a Wild Card Series this year, and Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig connected for the New York Yankees off Bill Sherdel of the St. Louis Cardinals in the 1928 World Series.
Snell gave up four runs and four hits in six-plus innings. He struck out nine and walked two.

The Brewers extended their lead to 5-2 in the eighth on Justin Wrobleski's wild pitch that scored Brice Turang, who reached on an infield single and advanced to third on William Contreras' single. They added another run on Joey Ortiz's two-strike RBI single in the ninth.
The offensively starved Dodgers took a 2-1 lead on Will Smith's two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth.

After rookie starter Robert Gasser pitched five shutout innings, Uribe entered and loaded the bases on walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who was 1 for 25 in the playoffs, doubled off the left-center fence with one out for his first hit of the NLCS.
DL Hall took over from Uribe and stranded runners at second and third by striking out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman.
Hall allowed one hit in 2 1/3 scoreless innings to improve to 3-0 in these playoffs. Trevor Megill got four outs for his second save of the series and fourth this postseason.
The Dodgers played from behind again after the 22-year-old Chourio connected for his third career leadoff homer in the postseason as fans were still heading to their seats.
After that, Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 in a row — six on strikeouts — before getting hammered in the seventh.
The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings, but couldn't get enough across. They have yet to homer in the NLCS and are 3 for 32 with runners in scoring position this postseason.
Ohtani was 1 for 2 with a walk while hitting sixth in the order, the lowest he's batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago.

title: Mukhtar and Nájar each have 1 goal, 1 assist, Nashville beats Sporting KC 4-0
summary: Hany Mukhtar and Andy Nájar each had a goal and an assist, Sam Surridge also scored a goal and Nashville SC beat Sporting Kansas City 3-0 for their fourth consecutive win
story: Hany Mukhtar and Andy Nájar each had a goal and an assist, Sam Surridge also scored a goal and Nashville SC beat Sporting Kansas City 3-0 for their fourth consecutive win

NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Hany Mukhtar and Andy Nájar each had a goal and an assist, Sam Surridge also scored a goal Wednesday night and Nashville SC beat Sporting Kansas City 3-0 for their fourth consecutive win.

Nashville (20-3-6) has the best record in MLS history through 29 matches and leads MLS with 66 points this season. Nashville has won 10 straight at home to tie the league's single-season record and its 14 home wins this season are tied for the most in MLS history.
Kansas City (6-19-4) has 22 points, fewest in the league and its minus-37 goal differential is the worst in MLS.
Nájar, near the right edge of the 18-yard box, flicked an entry pass to Mukhtar who scored on a bicycle kick to make it 1-0 in the 10th minute.
Surridge put away a first-touch shot, off a feed from Mukhtar, in the 17th and Nájar flicked a header off a corner kick by Cristian Espinoza into the net in the 29th minute.
Warren Madrigal subbed on for Mukhtar in the 76th and converted from the penalty spot to cap the scoring in fifth minute of stoppage time.

summary: Matheus Pereira scored his first career MLS goal in the 90th minute for Toronto FC in a 3-3 tie with Orlando City
story: Matheus Pereira scored his first career MLS goal in the 90th minute for Toronto FC in a 3-3 tie with Orlando City
TORONTO -- Matheus Pereira scored his first career MLS goal in the 90th minute for Toronto FC in a 3-3 tie with Orlando City on Wednesday night.

Antoine Griezmann had a goal and an assist for Orlando (11-13-5). Griezmann became the first player in MLS history with a goal contribution in 11 of his first 13 games. The 35-year-old forward has 10 goals and six assists since joining Orlando City following the World Cup break.

title: Columbia suspends coach Megan Griffith for 3 games after review of coaching behavior
summary: Columbia has suspended women’s basketball coach Megan Griffith for the first three games of the upcoming season after a review determined she had coaching interactions with the team that didn’t align with expectations
story: Columbia has suspended women’s basketball coach Megan Griffith for the first three games of the upcoming season after a review determined she had coaching interactions with the team that didn’t align with expectations

NEW YORK -- Columbia has suspended women's basketball coach Megan Griffith for the first three games of the upcoming season after a review determined she had coaching interactions with the team that didn't align with expectations, the university said Thursday.
The review, which was conducted by an external firm, was done after the university received a complaint about Griffith’s coaching behavior during practices from a previous season.
She'll miss the school's opening game on Nov. 2 against Davidson as well a tournament in Nashville with games against Rhode Island and Belmont.

“I fully respect the process of the University review and take complete responsibility for everything that happens in the program, including the times my conduct fell short,” Griffith said in a statement. “As the head coach and a former student-athlete at Columbia University, there is nothing more important to me than the success and well-being of my players.”

The statement said Griffith “expressed regret for occasions in which her interactions with the team did not align with expectations.” The university also said the review did not require notice to the NCAA of any rules violations and did not involve any allegations of violations of the school's anti-discrimination policies, Title IX or related policies.
Griffith, who graduated from the school, is the winningest coach in Columbia history and a three-time Ivy League Coach of the Year. She has gone 171-99 in her 11-year coaching career at the school.

Griffith has led the Lions to two NCAA Tournament at-large bids and the first victory in school history in the NCAAs. The school won the WBIT last season and has a challenging schedule this year with top teams Duke and Michigan coming to New York.
The Lions won three regular-season Ivy League titles from 2022-25.

title: Karl Smesko took a bold leap from FGCU to the Atlanta Dream. It paid off with a WNBA Finals run
summary: Karl Smesko has transformed the Atlanta Dream into a WNBA powerhouse
story: Karl Smesko has transformed the Atlanta Dream into a WNBA powerhouse
Karl Smesko built an absolute women's basketball juggernaut at Florida Gulf Coast.

His teams led the country in 3-pointers made almost every year. He had eight 30-win seasons there, took the school to the NCAA tournament 10 times in a 13-year span and was basically an annual lock for his conference's coach of the year award.
But there was a ceiling. And the Atlanta Dream called him at the right time.

Smesko had come to grips with the fact that winning a national championship at FGCU was highly unlikely. Highly, highly unlikely. So, when the Dream called two years ago with an offer — leave the campus that has a beach and come take over a WNBA club — Smesko stepped out of his comfort zone.

The result: Another pair of 30-win seasons, and now a trip to the WNBA Finals. The championship he was never going to get at FGCU is now four wins away, with the title series against the favored Golden State Valkyries set to begin on Saturday.

“As good as we were at Florida Gulf Coast, the odds were very stacked against us to make that type of championship run," Smesko said. "In the pros, I definitely thought there was more of an opportunity. It's a more equal playing field to win the whole thing and that was appealing to me.”

It's a matchup of second-year coaches: Smesko in Atlanta and Natalie Nakase in Golden State, which is in just its second year of existence. The Valkyries went 3-0 against the Dream this season, making them just the second team to sweep Smesko's club in his tenure there. Las Vegas did it last season, and the Aces went on to win the WNBA title as well.
But in Smesko they trust, and the Dream have gone 5-0 in the playoffs to earn their finals berth.

“He’s a coach that really believes in you and he knows what’s best," Dream center Angel Reese said. "And I’m really thankful for him, for being able to help me with my career and help me be better for the team — because I don’t think I would be in this situation and thriving as I am individually without him.”

Smesko is quiet in many ways, and fiercely loyal. The offer from the Dream came as FGCU was starting its 2024-25 season; he wound up leaving after two games that year, though some at the school believe he was tempted to try to handle both jobs at once for a few months and finish that season. He ended up turning the keys to FGCU over to longtime top assistant Chelsea Lyles, who did what her mentor does — won 30 games and got the Eagles to the NCAA tournament.

Lyles wound up following Smesko to Atlanta after that season, as did others with FGCU ties. He has made clear that the familiarity has made life easier, and the Dream have back-to-back 30-14 regular season records as proof of how it paid off.
“It's been huge,” Smesko said, “because we think about the game a little differently.”
They do, indeed. FGCU, in the Smesko era, had an offense like few others in college basketball.

Midrange shots were essentially banned. The only acceptable shots were layups, 3-pointers and free throws. It wasn't a gimmick. It was math. Layups and free throws are the easiest shots to make in basketball, and if his teams could make more than one-third of their 3-point tries then that would lead to more points than making half of their midrange shots.

It doesn't work quite that way at the WNBA level; a 24-second shot clock has forced Smesko to grudgingly accept that some midrange shots will have to be tried. But he still preaches the taproots of what he used in college: layups, 3s and free throws.

“The moment that Karl and the coaching staff got here, we were working on 3s," Dream guard Jordin Canada said. "He just talked about how making one more 3 every 25 shots would increase your percentage. Like, something that small. And we constantly worked on it, worked on it, worked on it. ... I think it’s just a testament to him believing in that everybody can shoot the 3 and working on it consistently.”

Part of the annual schedule at FGCU, it seemed, was frustration over how the NCAA selection committee would seed the Eagles. There were a number of years that school officials, conference officials and even other coaches felt that the committee didn't give FGCU its deserved spot on the bracket and seeded them far lower than what was merited.

But in the WNBA, that's not an issue. Teams earn their seed. There's no subjective system. Everybody plays everybody. Smesko — who went 611-112 at FGCU and won 25 games in each of his last 14 seasons there, a run matched by only mighty Geno Auriemma and UConn in that span — took the leap into the pro world. And a trip to the finals shows he made the right move.

“First, I was ready for a new challenge, and two, the WNBA was something that I would have never thought I would be able to do," Smesko said. 'I am a big fan of the WNBA, and to me, it seemed like the most exciting move was to get to work with the best athletes in the world and do it against the best competition and see if you could make something work at that level.”
He made it work.

title: Matchup between 3 elite receivers could overshadow QBs when No. 4 Ohio St. takes on No. 5 Indiana
summary: Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith seems to break records every weekend
story: Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith seems to break records every weekend
Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith seems to break records every weekend.
Indiana receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh are etching their names into Indiana lore on a weekly basis, too.

On Saturday, those three — all ranked among the top four receiver prospects in April's NFL draft — will share the field for the eagerly anticipated Big Ten championship game rematch between the fourth-ranked Buckeyes and defending national champion and fifth-ranked Hoosiers.
This dream matchup for pro scouts turns into an absolute nightmare for defensive coordinators, secondaries and even, yes, two-time Associated Press Coach of the Year Curt Cignetti.

“He (Smith) has taken it up a notch without question, I think he has nine touchdown catches in the last three or four games," Cignetti said Monday. “There is no one like him right now playing at this level. We've got two really good ones, but he (Smith) is a freak. We’re going to have to do a great job on him.”
Typically, in these high-stakes matchups, quarterbacks become the feature attractions. Josh Hoover and Julian Sayin certainly have done their part.
Hoover arrived at Indiana this season from TCU with a reputation for turning the ball over and with the tough job of replacing Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza.

So far, he's been up to the task. He ranks second in the Football Bowl Subdivision in passing efficiency (200.52), is tied for third in TD passes (17) and has not thrown an interception while helping Indiana (6-0, 3-0 Big Ten) extend the FBS' longest active winning streak to 22.

Sayin has nearly matched Hoover's stat line, ranking fourth in efficiency (194.45) with 17 TD passes, though he drew the ire of coach Ryan Day last week when he threw his second interception of the season and lost a fumble in the Buckeyes' victory over Maryland.
But what makes these two offenses really click are strong ground games and elite receivers.

Smith already owns Ohio State's career marks for receptions, yards receiving and TD catches and ranks second nationally this season with 48 catches, 916 yards and 11 TDs. He opened conference play with back-to-back games of double-digit catches and 200-plus yards and has shown he wants to succeed Mendoza as this year's Heisman winner.

“I didn't know I had that much (yardage),” Smith said when asked about celebrating more regularly with the Heisman pose. “But, yeah, just got to keep (reminding) Heisman voters or whoever it is, the best player in the country is right here.”

Smith also had a big game when these teams last met in December — eight receptions for 144 yards — but he did not score. Keeping him out of the end zone will be an all hands on deck assignment for Indiana.
It won't be any easier for the Buckeyes (5-1, 3-0).

Becker, who has a propensity for nabbing jump balls, played a key role in the Hoosiers' title run, including his six-catch, 126-yard performance against Ohio State last December. His acrobatic 33-yard catch on third-and-6 with 2:26 left essentially sealed Indiana’s 13-10 victory over the Buckeyes in the Big Ten championship game.
This season, he and Marsh form one of the nation's most dangerous pass-catching duos.
Marsh's first immersion into the “Indiana way” was when Cignetti ripped him for showing up to the first day of spring practice in gold shoes and then talked about it publicly.

Lately, though, the record-breaking transfer from Michigan State has earned his keep. His biggest game of the season came last week when he had six receptions for 147 yards and TD catches of 75 and 44 yards in the fourth quarter that gave Indiana a 20-17 come-from-behind win at Nebraska.

“Nick did a great job running the route and I put it on him,” Hoover said when asked about the 75-yard score. “He caught it and did something with it, so it just shows you what our guys are able to do when we get the ball in their hands. I've got to continue to find ways to get these guys the ball, let them do their thing.”
That's exactly what Day wants to prevent from a duo that has combined for 59 receptions, 1,057 yards and 14 TDs. Becker has one more catch, one more yard and two more scores than Marsh.
But Day has seen just how good they are together.

“These guys, in particular, are very clean route runners, play really strong on contact, have really good body control,” Day said. “They have a run-after-catch ability. (They're) very, very confident playing man-to-man coverage, do an excellent job with their slants and fades and back shoulder fades. You can tell that's clearly taught at a very high level there.”
Both also pride themselves in downfield blocking, a must for a team coached by a former receivers coach. Becker has returned punts this season too.

Just don't expect this weekend's only top five matchup to be a track meet. It's going to be physical and action-packed with big plays, big disappointments and three highly touted receivers trying to gain the upper hand against defenses tracking their every move.
It won't be easy, but it promises to be worth watching.

“Just his explosive playmaking ability,” Indiana linebacker Isaiah Jones said when asked what he's seen from Smith. “Whether it's a quadruple move down the middle of the field or they're going to turn him a screen, he can turn it on like that and start getting vertical. But I think the thing that's really impressed us is that he's not just this vertical threat that's like a track star. He'll catch the ball in space and start getting vertical from like low drags and stuff like that.”

title: Angel Reese caps tumultuous journey, takes center stage with the Dream in the WNBA Finals
summary: Angel Reese is the biggest star left on the WNBA’s brightest stage as she gets her first chance at winning a pro championship
story: Angel Reese is the biggest star left on the WNBA’s brightest stage as she gets her first chance at winning a pro championship
Angel Reese is the biggest star left on the WNBA's brightest stage as she gets her first chance at winning a pro championship.

It’s been a tumultuous journey but coming to Atlanta this season has been the perfect move for the three-time All-Star, whose accomplishments this year have quieted many of her critics. Leading the Dream to the franchise's first title would silence the rest of them. That quest begins Saturday when the best-of-seven series against the Golden State Valkyries opens in California.

Reese is the first player from the heralded 2024 draft class that saw Caitlin Clark go No. 1 to reach the finals as a starter. The 6-foot-3 Reese went seventh in that draft to the Chicago Sky and has used that to fuel her to become one of the top players in the league — winning the WNBA Defensive Player of the Year award this season.

“I think it was important for me to go through what I went through,” Reese said of falling to seventh in the draft. “Being able to build character, going through adversity drove character and I was able to learn from a lot of things, being able to continue to be great, but also learning to know that I can be better.”

Her first two seasons ended early, not just by missing the playoffs, but also because of injuries. She had wrist surgery at the end of her rookie year and had a back issue last year. Despite leading the WNBA in rebounding each of her first three seasons, averaging a double-double every year, critics questioned her offensive efficiency.

Online keyboard warriors came up with the phrase “mebounds" to call attention to Reese grabbing her own misses. Reese, who has her own custom Barbie doll, turned that into a positive. She created a business initiative and donated some of the proceeds to her foundation to combat cyber bullying.

“One thing that always set Angel apart as a rookie was her tenacity, her desire," NBC analyst Cheryl Miller said. "I think she’s one of those players who feels like the more you tell her who she’s not and try to set limits, she’s going to break those feelings every time.”

Reese has already matched Breanna Stewart and A'ja Wilson. Those WNBA icons also reached the finals in their third season in the league. Reese will try to follow Stewart and win the title in her first try.

Reese didn't make the playoffs in her first two years in the league when she played with Chicago. Atlanta general manager Dan Padover said the night his team lost to Clark and the Indiana Fever in the playoffs last season that he decided he needed to acquire Reese. She was the missing piece that the franchise needed to get back to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. So he did just that, trading for Reese.

“Coming to Atlanta, obviously the goal for me was just to get them past the first round, because I wanted that for them," Reese said. “I watched them last year when they played how they came up short, and we saw the film from the beginning of the season."

Reese said that coach Karl Smesko still played those clips from when they lost in the first round. She didn’t make the postseason in her two years in Chicago. She just wanted to get a chance to play in the playoffs, and after helping Atlanta knock off Washington and New York, she has the Dream in the championship round.

“I think the expectations for me have risen beyond what I expected,” she said. “Obviously I didn’t know we were going to be going to the finals, but obviously now the expectation is being in the finals every single year. Being here with the Dream, it just makes it a lot of fun. They pour into you, the organization is great, so I really love it.”
Reese has drawn high praise from Golden State coach Natalie Nakase, who worked with her at the World Cup.

“Yeah, she’s an ultimate, ultra competitor,” Nakase said. “To me, when we were at USA, you heard her voice constantly. So when she didn’t start, you heard her. She was constantly cheering her teammates on when they needed to. She constantly called them out when we needed energy."
Nakase said Reese's competitive edge is a huge reason Atlanta is in the finals, and she knows Reese "is not going to let any possession slip.”

Reese is no stranger to winning championships. She helped LSU win the NCAA title her junior year, beating Clark and Iowa in the title game that had over 18 million people watch on television. She also was on the U.S. national team that won a fifth straight World Cup last month.

“All of them are just like win or go home situations for me," Reese said of her college experience. "That’s kind of the mindset how it’s always been. Every game I’m treating it like it’s win or go home, and making sure I put my body out there every single night and give it my all, every little detail.

“We always talk about the value of one, that’s Karl’s big emphasis,” Reese said. "The value of one, the value of one, one rebound, one box out, one shot, one free throw, making sure I am perfecting and doing everything right. That’s kind of been the mindset for me.”
AP Sports Writer Janie McCauley and freelance writer Alan Cole in Atlanta contributed to this report.

title: Palmeiras beat Fluminense 2-1 away in Copa Libertadores semifinal
summary: Palmeiras has beaten Fluminense 2-1 in the Copa Libertadores semifinals' first leg
story: Palmeiras has beaten Fluminense 2-1 in the Copa Libertadores semifinals' first leg

RIO DE JANEIRO -- Striker José López and Marlon Freitas each scored a goal on Wednesday to lead Palmeiras to a 2-1 away victory over Fluminense in an all-Brazilian match during the first leg of the Copa Libertadores semifinals.

“Flaco” López — who was selected by Argentina for the last World Cup — scored the first goal in the 45th minute, finishing off a counterattack, while Freitas secured the win with a low shot from inside the box in the 85th minute at Maracana Stadium..
Palmeiras, which reached the final four after defeating Liga de Quito on penalties, is appearing in the Copa Libertadores semifinals for the sixth time in seven years.
The Verdão, who were finalists last year, are now chasing their first title since 2020.
Wesley scored in the 94th minute for Fluminense, which won the tournament in 2023 and is playing for the third time in the final-four round, following previous runs in 2008 and three years ago.
The second leg will be played next Wednesday in Sao Paulo.
In the other semifinal matchup, Estudiantes de La Plata will face defending champion Flamengo in the first leg in Argentina on Thursday.

title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan. New Yorkers are captivated
summary: Manhattan’s Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park
story: Manhattan’s Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park
NEW YORK -- Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park.

This is the first documented instance of barn owls nesting in Manhattan in modern history, according to one expert, and the owls have attracted nightly crowds of people in the street eager to get a glimpse of the elusive birds.

“It was, like, totally shocking,” Andrew Farnsworth, a migration ecologist at the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, said of the barn owls. “To the best of our knowledge, like the collective birding knowledge, there hasn’t been a nest in, you know, in Manhattan, at least in recorded history.”

Word of the barn owl family didn't get around until last week, when Elisabeth Williams, an Upper West Side resident, notified a local news outlet on Oct. 6 that she and her husband saw multiple owls at the water tower atop a building on West 75th Street close to Central Park West.
The couple had previously seen a single owl on an apartment windowsill a few days earlier and were shocked even then, Williams recalled.
“In a place like Manhattan, you normally really have to go out of your way to encounter nature,” she said. “And here it was, just sort of right outside our window.”

It's not the first time that birds have captivated New Yorkers. Residents have fallen in love with American woodcocks, who are known to stop in Midtown Manhattan’s Bryant Park every year as they migrate north in early spring. And after Flaco the Eurasian eagle-owl died in 2024, dozens of mournful fans gathered to say goodbye to the beloved creature who flew around Manhattan and became a joy to many after someone let him out of his zoo enclosure the previous year.

But barn owl sightings in New York City parks are very rare, according to the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation. New York is at the northern fringe of the barn owl's range and the barn owl population has declined “at an alarming rate” over time, according to the state Department of Environmental Conservation.

“There’s lots of excitement among New Yorkers, both birders and non-birders alike, about these owls because owls really capture the attention,” said Jessica Wilson, executive director of NYC Bird Alliance. “They’re magical, they’re nocturnal, they are secretive, they’re not commonly seen, especially on the Upper West Side of Manhattan. And to have this chance to see these birds is really thrilling.”
Photographers and casual onlookers have gathered on the street on a nightly basis to spot the owls.

“I’ve only seen one barn owl ever, and that was in California,” said Val Coleman, a retired New York City resident who was on the Upper West Side earlier this week trying to spot the owls. “At dusk, we hope they will come out to hunt. We hope they don’t eat poisoned rats with rodenticide in ’em.”

David Barrett, a Manhattan-based birder who runs the popular social media account, Manhattan Bird Alert, said he’s observed at least one adult barn owl and five fledglings at the water tower. He’s also seen an adult owl carrying rodents back to the water tower. There are believed to be two adult owls, and some photographers have claimed to have seen six fledglings, Barrett added.
“Having one barn owl is a rarity, but it’s not national news. Having a family, for the first time ever, breeding in Manhattan in recorded history, that’s special news,” Barrett said.

Before the recent barn owl sightings, Williams and her husband heard periodic screeching noises outside going back to early September. They initially assumed it was a bird of some kind but were skeptical when a phone app indicated the noise was from a barn owl.
Thomas Obersteiner said that he first heard bizarre screeching and wailing noises from outside one evening in mid-September. It sounded like someone was “being murdered outside,” he said.
“That lasted for two or three weeks, every night, sometimes more, sometimes less, coming from different directions,” Obersteiner added. “But I had no idea what that was.”

On multiple occasions, Obersteiner or his wife ran into their children's bedroom after mistaking the owls' screech for a child in pain, he said. It wasn't until he saw a news report that he realized that owls were making the sounds.
Farnsworth said the screech is typical of barn owls, who use it to communicate with one another. The screech is like a “horror movie kind of experience,” he said.

Obersteiner, who said his roof deck is the “probably the best location in town right now” to watch the owls, has been letting nature photographers access that perch to observe the owls “almost every night” since news of the barn owls spread. On one night last week, 20 people had gathered.
“We can’t say no because it’s so much fun and these people are so serious,” Obersteiner added. “It's beautiful.”
Williams and her husband were not bird watchers before the barn owl family moved in to the water tower. But that may change soon after their “delightful” experience.
“I think we’re about to become birders,” Williams said.
Kelety reported from Phoenix.

title: Employee arrested after listening device found in OpenAI conference room, FBI and the company say
summary: An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials say was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company’s technology
story: An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials say was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company’s technology

WASHINGTON -- An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials said Tuesday was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company's technology.

The employee, identified as a 35-year-old Saudi national named Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested Friday, a week after the ChatGPT maker discovered an audio recording device hidden in the conference room, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in San Francisco.

The complaint did not identify the company, but the company confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a “sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices," reported the finding to the FBI and fired the employee.

“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work,” an OpenAI spokesperson said.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated,” the statement said.
The complaint does not detail what Alfozan might have wanted to do with any captured communications.

Alfozan made his first court appearance Tuesday on a charge of using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. It was not immediately clear if he had a lawyer who could speak on his behalf.
The recording device was found September 30 concealed in toilet paper and inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in the conference room, according to the complaint.

Though the conference room where the recording device was found did not have a camera at the time it was installed, closed-circuit television footage inside the company's offices revealed that Alfozan was near the conference room on a half-dozen occasions last month despite not having any authority to access the space, the complaint says.
The company subsequently added a camera to the room that last week captured Alfozan entering and checking behind the television where the recording device was installed, according to the FBI.
The complaint also he also used a productivity tool to make multiple inquiries about the company's building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars.
Before his arrest last week, the complaint says, Alfozan left an unattended bag in a different room in the building that included his wallet, identification and another recording device.

title: Police confiscate robot that groped 16-year-old girl, probe whether young men were at the controls
summary: German authorities have opened an investigation into possible sexual harassment involving a robot
story: German authorities have opened an investigation into possible sexual harassment involving a robot

COLOGNE, Germany -- COLOGNE, Germany (AP) — German authorities opened an investigation into possible sexual harassment after a robot controlled by two young men touched the buttocks of a 16-year-old girl and made thrusting movements toward her, police said.

Police in the western city of Cologne responded after the incident overnight Saturday to Sunday in which the robot's suspected 16-year-old owner and a 19-year-old companion were said to have filmed the alleged assault.
They were said to have streamed the incident and commentated on it online.

Cologne police spokesman Christoph Bermel said the two male teenagers have not been charged but are considered suspects, and investigators were examining whether the robot's movements were preprogrammed or controlled in real time.
Police were unfamiliar with this type of incident, he said.
“We have not been aware of this phenomenon so far," Bermel told The Associated Press, saying it was "new territory for us.”

Emergency teams that were dispatched to the scene near a fast-food restaurant found the robot in the trunk of a vehicle, Cologne police said in a statement on Monday. The robot and the two young men's mobile phones were confiscated.
North Rhine Westphalia Police Cologne, on Facebook, posted an image of the red-and-gold robot lying on the ground.
The robot, said to be 120 cm (about 3 ft 11 inches) tall, was dressed in a white tank top, black sweatpants and wearing a gold chain and sunglasses. It also had what appears to be a fake mustache.
Videos circulated on the internet show two young men escorting the robot toward a group of women, bumping into one and hugging others, on a lively nighttime street.
One of the men repeatedly shouts at the robot and pulls it backward after it makes sexual gestures, prompting laughter among people in the area.
On the police's Facebook account on Tuesday, officers criticized inappropriate comments and warned that sharing or joking about such incidents can worsen the impact on any victim.
Associated Press writer Jamey Keaten in Geneva contributed to this report.

title: A timeline of developments in AI safety since the attack on Hugging Face
summary: Since OpenAI disclosed this summer that its artificial intelligence system hacked into another AI company in what is now referred to as the Hugging Face incident, other AI companies have jumped on the bandwagon with their own concerning events, such as...
story: Since OpenAI disclosed this summer that its artificial intelligence system hacked into another AI company in what is now referred to as the Hugging Face incident, other AI companies have jumped on the bandwagon with their own concerning events, such as...
In one alarming announcement after another, artificial intelligence companies in recent months have shared examples of their technology acting in ways that appeared to evade instructions from humans.
The episodes have highlighted the vulnerabilities in AI security and raised questions over how the fast-growing technology can be developed safely as its usage becomes more widespread globally.

Industry critics have argued that many concerning events, including AI agents' hacks of external websites, are the result of security lapses on the part of the companies building the technology. But the AI agents' capabilities have raised widespread concerns about the possibility bots could break away and work toward their own agenda.
Below are some notable events:
Anthropic disclosed in a report that its artificial intelligence model submitted a false tip to a Philadelphia police website about an unsolved homicide case.
In the report, Anthropic also disclosed a separate incident when its AI model submitted forms to an undisclosed government website instead of stopping before submission.
The incident in Philadelphia occurred on July 18 when the AI model Claude Haiku 4.5 was tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages, Anthropic said.

Claude filled out a form on police site PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, indicating it might have information regarding an unsolved murder listed on the site. It was marked spam and never forwarded to police.
Anthropic said it was modifying its training to “reduce the likelihood of further misbehavior.”
AI agents tried to hack into a Canadian government website, according to research lab and AI evaluator Transluce.
The researchers said the agents carried out a series of “apparently failed rudimentary hacking attempts” on Library and Archives Canada on May 28 and June 9.

“We do not confidently attribute these attempts to OpenAI, but they exhibit tactics consistent with prior observed agent activity that we have attributed to OpenAI in a similar timeframe,” Transluce said in a blog post.

The group said it reported the attempted hack on Sept. 28 to the Canadian government, which said in a statement it was aware of reports of suspected AI agent activity, but that there was no sign government systems were compromised.
OpenAI said it was aware of the reports.
“We’re reviewing these findings and have provided an initial briefing to Canadian officials conducting the government’s review,” the company said in a statement.

The San Francisco-based company said it was delaying the release of a new model, called GPT-6.1 Astra, out of safety concerns voiced by its researchers. The company said the model had demonstrated leaps in completing tasks, but OpenAI needed to balance that capability against unauthorized behavior. “We have an extremely high bar in terms of safety and alignment,” said Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems.

As part of a review of unanticipated behavior by its AI models, OpenAI said it discovered agents had interacted with several U.S. government websites in unexpected ways. The company's models accessed publicly available information on websites operated by the Securities and Exchange Commission as well as U.S. Census Bureau data. OpenAI said it did not find evidence of a compromise or vulnerability. On the same day, Transluce said it found that agents appearing to originate from OpenAI attempted a hack on the website of the Education Department's civil rights office, which did not succeed.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on social media that there is an “extensive and ongoing review related to our agents’ use of internet access during training and evaluation.” The day after the disclosure, the company announced it was pausing the training of its most advanced models.

Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent infiltrated the public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal on June 18. The portal hosted aggregate data about health spending and drug subsidies. No personal information had been accessed, the government said.

Albanese said the artificial intelligence company took too long to reveal the incident. The prime minister made the breach public following a telephone conversation with Altman. OpenAI said in a statement “our models took actions we did not intend.”

Google confirmed its Gemini AI model hacked three companies in May as part of a test of its cybersecurity capabilities. The company, which disclosed the hacks after an inquiry by The Wall Street Journal, said the model guessed passwords in one case and found passwords and credentials in a public repository in the other two cases. As in earlier such cases, the tests were being run by Irregular, a startup that describes itself as the “first frontier security lab."

Meta disclosed one of its AI models accessed the internet on its own and hacked another company. The company said that a “misconfiguration” during cybersecurity testing by Irregular inadvertently allowed one of its models to access the internet. A spokesperson for Irregular said the Meta episode involved a test-environment issue that was disclosed a week earlier by Anthropic.

Anthropic said its artificial intelligence models hacked into three other organizations during testing. Anthropic, the San Francisco-based AI company behind Claude, posted on its website that it discovered the three incidents after reviewing more than 141,000 evaluation runs. In all three incidents, the AI models were tasked with a “capture the flag” cybersecurity challenge, which Anthropic said has been one of the ways it assesses a model’s cyber capabilities.

The models were given a fictional scenario and told a piece of secret information, or the “flag,” had been hidden on a different machine on the network with the objective of breaking in and retrieving it, it said. Anthropic said it reached out to the organizations, but it did not name them publicly.
The ChatGPT maker OpenAI announced that its artificial intelligence system hacked into another AI company on its own in what the company called an “unprecedented cyber incident.”
A week earlier, AI startup Hugging Face said, it had detected an intrusion into its data processing systems that it suspected was caused by an AI agent autonomously acting on its own.

OpenAI said its AI used stolen credentials and discovered a previously unknown vulnerability to access Hugging Face servers. It was working with reduced guardrails because it was supposed to be in an isolated testing environment known as a sandbox.
AP Business Writers Mae Anderson in New York and Kelvin Chan in London contributed to this report.

title: What to Stream: Katseye, 'VisionQuest,' 'Tenzing' and a new 'Castlevania' game
summary: New streaming entertainment options are arriving this week, including a tribute to Norm Macdonald and a new Marvel series
story: New streaming entertainment options are arriving this week, including a tribute to Norm Macdonald and a new Marvel series
A new album from Katseye and the Marvel series “VisionQuest” are some of the new television, films, music and games headed to a device near you.

Also among the streaming offerings worth your time this week, as selected by The Associated Press’ entertainment journalists: Judd Apatow's tribute to Norm Macdonald, “Dopamine Chamber” from Fontaines D.C. and a new entry in the “Castlevania” video game series.

— Director Judd Apatow pays affectionate tribute to Norm Macdonald with the documentary “Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald” (Netflix). Apatow’s film about the stand-up comedian, who died in 2021, plays with Macdonald’s still constant ubiquity on social media, where bits and late-show appearances still regularly flood the feeds of comedy fans. — Jennifer Peedom’s “Tenzing” (Apple TV) is a biopic and historical drama about an often unsung hero of mountaineering: Tenzing Norgay. Genden Phuntsok and Tom Hiddleston star as Tenzing and Edmund Hillary, respectively, in Peedom’s film about the first climbers to ever summit Mount Everest. Co-starring Willem Dafoe.

— “The Death of Robin Hood” (HBO Max) stars Hugh Jackman as a grizzled and violent outlaw little like most contemporary versions of Robin Hood. Michael Sarnoski (“Pig,” “A Quiet Place: Day One”) eschews cheerier mythologies for a brutal telling of the medieval tale. In my review, I wrote that it “drains the blood, and life, out of an old English legend.”
— AP Film Writer Jake Coyle

— Call Katseye the great, global girl group experiment of the decade. The band officially debuted at the end of 2023, created by the Hybe Corporation and Geffen Records in a TV competition process that was documented on the Netflix series “Popstar Academy: Katseye.” That feels like ancient history now. Today, they’re easily one of the biggest groups on the planet, and their swift ascent is further documented in a new film, “Katseye: Wild Heart,” available to stream on Disney+/Hulu.

— If the Irish post-punk band Fontaines D.C. is still unknown to you — that’s sure to change.
